summary: SSE session shadowing leads to interleaved partial fragments and duplicated segments after reconnection
description: Issue summary: Customer reports that, after an SSE disconnect and reconnect, the new stream occasionally receives interleaved partial fragments that appear to contain leftover bytes from the previous connection; fragments are duplicated and out of order, producing malformed JSON events in the client. Impact: NoteStream's document-collaboration feature intermittently shows duplicated paragraphs and garbled JSON choices in ~4% of long-running sessions (clients holding streams >8 minutes).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use a long-running SSE stream against /v1/stream with model open/gpt-medium-v2 and a prompt that yields multi-paragraph output (~1500 tokens).
2) Simulate an edge flake: send TCP RST from client after ~5 minutes, then immediately reconnect with a fresh SSE subscribe using same client session id header (x-session-id).

3) Observe the newly opened stream frames in the browser or curl; check for interleaved partials that contain JSON fragments starting mid-object (e.g., '...,"text":"paragraph') and duplicated sentence fragments before a final end event.
expected_behavior: After reconnect, the new SSE stream should only contain events corresponding to the new connection; any prior stream should be fully closed and not leak partial fragments. JSON event boundaries must remain intact and finalization markers should not be duplicated.
actual_behavior: New SSE stream occasionally receives: 1) partial JSON fragments that concatenate with new fragments producing invalid JSON, 2) duplicated text segments (prior sentence appears again mid-output), and 3) 'ghost' metadata events with stale request ids. Client sees parsing errors and duplicated paragraphs.
logs: edge-proxy (nginx) access log excerpt: 10.12.5.82 - - [12/Mar/2026:14:22:08 +0000] "GET /v1/stream HTTP/1.1" 200 - "-" "sse" x-session-id=abc-123
serving-runtime trace (request id req-88b1): last-send=2026-03-12T14:21:57Z, connection-reset-detected=true, buffered-bytes=1843
application error (client): JSON.parse error at byte 764 - unexpected token at start of object
investigation_notes: 2026-03-12 15:00 - Support (Maya): Collected customer logs, asked for a pcap and HTTP trace; customer provided curl replay and proxy logs.

2026-03-12 16:10 - SRE (Oliver): Reproduced locally with our nginx + keepalive/buffer settings by simulating abrupt client close; saw leftover buffer flushed into new connection when upstream sent tail after proxy forwarded new request. Hypothesis: edge proxy connection pooling + upstream write-window causes 'shadowed' bytes to be appended to newly established SSE stream if sockets are recycled too quickly.

2026-03-12 17:05 - Runtime (Priya): Checked serving-runtime behavior: runtime marks stream closed on socket level but some internal response buffer (for long-running generation) can leak if downstream connection transitions use the same worker and buffered bytes are not fully drained before a new request attaches to the worker (rare race under bursty reconnects).

2026-03-12 18:30 - Networking (Diego): Confirmed NLB health-probe and proxy keepalive settings: idle_timeout 60s, proxy_buffering on, reuse_port enabled. Observed pattern when client reconnects within 200ms of server write, upstream sends trailing chunk which is still queued in proxy buffer and is forwarded into the new downstream connection (session shadowing).
Telemetry: Affected sessions spike on customer-hosted dedicated pool when they use aggressive client reconnects from mobile clients that switch networks.
mitigation_steps: 1) Instruct customer to set client-side reconnect backoff: avoid immediate reconnect within 500ms after abrupt close.
2) Disable proxy_buffering temporarily for the customer's route (config change applied to their dedicated gateway) to prevent queued bytes from being reused across sockets.
3) Add temporary server-side filter that ensures worker socket buffers are drained/cleared before reusing worker for new connections (hotfix deployed to dedicated cluster for NoteStream).
resolution: Hotfix deployed 2026-03-13: runtime worker now enforces buffer drain semantics before worker reuse; edge gateway route updated to disable proxy_buffering for the customer's dedicated domain. Customer validated with long-running sessions and aggressive reconnect tests; duplication rate dropped from ~4% to <0.1%. Follow-up: engineering to land a durable fix in runtime's connection teardown path and add an integration test simulating abrupt reconnects behind proxy. See PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2231.
postmortem_followups: 1) Engineering ticket INT-331210: Add automated fuzz/integration tests for SSE reconnect semantics behind proxy (owner: Priya).
2) Ops runbook update: include guidance to disable proxy_buffering for long-lived streaming routes (owner: Diego).
3) Customer success: schedule a short call to review recommended client reconnect backoff and verify monitoring alerts (owner: Maya).
